questions.q: What are the three separate engineering problems hidden in the registrar's one-sentence request?
options: Choosing a database platform, writing a style guide, and naming the application
Instance strategy and promotion, verified test coverage, and a hard deployment-timing constraint
Picking a logo, writing a press release, and scheduling a demo
Hiring more registrar staff, buying new hardware, and renaming the spreadsheet
questions.explain: "Tested before it goes live" and "cannot break during peak enrollment" map directly onto ATF coverage and deployment timing, layered on top of a real Dev/Test/Prod pipeline.

questions.q: Why does this capstone treat the three-instance Dev/Test/Prod pipeline as non-negotiable rather than optional overhead?
options: The registrar's office specifically asked for extra instances as a vanity feature
It's the only way to actually prove "tested before it goes live" instead of just asserting it
It has nothing to do with testing and exists only for licensing reasons
ServiceNow requires exactly three instances for every scoped application by default
questions.explain: A direct-to-Prod "quick fix" has no record anywhere else and creates drift immediately — the three-instance pipeline from Chapter 1 is what makes verifiable testing possible at all.

questions.q: Why does the registrar's IT director specifically want this application connected to Git-based Source Control?
options: Because Update Sets are being deprecated by ServiceNow and no longer work
To make the application run faster in production
To get a reviewable paper trail of every change, after a past vendor made undocumented changes nobody could explain later
Git is required for ATF tests to run at all
questions.explain: Git history turns every change into a reviewable diff with a pull request, directly answering the director's "paper trail" requirement from Chapter 3's connection pattern.

questions.q: In this capstone's design, what is the relationship between the CI/CD pipeline and Change Management?
options: Change Management only applies to the Dev instance, never to Test or Prod
The pipeline doesn't replace Change Management — every Test-to-Prod promotion is still gated by a Change Request, now with the ATF Test Suite's result attached as evidence
The Change Advisory Board is removed entirely once ATF tests exist
The CI/CD pipeline fully replaces the need for any Change Request
questions.explain: Chapter 5's resolution of the velocity-vs-control tension is to feed the Change Advisory Board better, faster evidence — not to bypass the Change Request process.

questions.q: What specific constraint from Chapter 6 makes this capstone a genuine engineering problem rather than a routine build?
options: Three annual peak enrollment weeks during which the application cannot be down, mid-deployment, or subject to any planned change
A requirement that the application have no database tables of its own
A rule that only one developer may ever touch the Dev instance
A requirement that the application be rewritten in a different programming language
questions.explain: Every deployment window and rollback plan in this capstone has to be built around avoiding those three peak weeks — "we'll figure out rollback if something breaks" isn't acceptable when registration itself is what could break.
